title: An ample module over an affine base gives separated canonical Proj data
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes with $T$ affine [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then for every affine open $W\subseteq T$, the restriction $L|_{f^{-1}(W)}$ is ample. Moreover, $f$ is separated and quasi-separated [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The canonical section algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes d}$ is a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], where $f_*L^{\otimes d}(W)=\Gamma(f^{-1}(W),L^{\otimes d})$ and tensor powers use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Its adjunction evaluation $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L^{\otimes d}$ uses module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $U(\psi)$ is the union, for $d\geq1$, of the open loci where $\psi_d$ is surjective, then $U(\psi)=X$, and the canonical morphism $r_{L,\psi}:X\to\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ is an open immersion [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map, def-nagata-relative-proj, def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tags 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), affine-base part of (3) implies (5); 01VI (lemma-relatively-ample-separated); 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample)(2), affine specialization.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $W\subseteq T$. The inclusion $j:W\to T$ is affine by lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine, since both schemes are affine. Its base change $g:f^{-1}(W)\to X$ is affine by lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence(1). Apply lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible to $g$ and the given ample $L$: $g^*L$ is ample. For this open inclusion, the pullback formula $\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(W)}\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_X}g^{-1}L$ identifies $g^*L$ with $L|_{f^{-1}(W)}$, since $g^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(W)}$ and the tensor unit acts by multiplication. This proves the restriction clause for every $W$.

source.place: Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample)(2), using its existing affine-pullback specialization; Tag 01SH (lemma-morphism-affines-affine).

proof.text: By lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated the structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. It is the composite of $f$ with the structure map of $T$. Hence lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation(b) makes $f$ separated. Then lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated makes $f$ quasi-separated. Thus the assumed quasi-compactness and the just-proved quasi-separatedness are available before constructing the section algebra.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), affine-base separatedness in (3) implies (5); properties.tex Tag 09MP (lemma-ample-separated).

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-qcqs-line-section-algebra-evaluation to $f$ and $L$. It gives the quasi-coherent graded algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes d}$, its evaluation $\psi$, and its canonical map $r:U(\psi)\to P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$. Take the affine base open $T$ itself in that lemma and put $S=\Gamma_*(X,L)$. Its specified identifications give $\mathcal A(T)=S$, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, and $U(\psi)=\bigcup_{d>0,s\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes d})}X_s$. Ampleness says that every $x\in X$ belongs to an affine $X_s$ of positive degree, so this union is $X$. The same lemma identifies $r$ under $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ with the usual canonical map for the identity graded map of $S$. The direct-image formula on each affine $W$ is exactly the formula in that lemma.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), (3) implies (5), section algebra and generation locus; constructions.tex Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj)(3).

proof.text: Consider all positive-degree sections $s$ for which $X_s$ is affine. They cover $X$ by the definition of ampleness. By lem-sc-ample-proj-local-chart, the canonical map $a:X\to\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ satisfies $a^{-1}(D_+(s))=X_s$ for every positive-degree homogeneous $s$, and its restriction $a_s:X_s\to D_+(s)$ is an isomorphism for every section in this cover. The canonical map here is the identity-section-ring map identified with $r$ in step 3, not an arbitrary open immersion into some Proj. Let $V=\bigcup_{X_s\text{ affine}}D_+(s)$. The inverse-image equalities and the cover show that the image of $a$ is exactly $V$.

The map $a$ is injective: if $a(x)=a(y)$, choose a covering section $s$ with $x\in X_s$; then $a(x)\in D_+(s)$, the inverse-image equality forces $y\in X_s$, and injectivity of $a_s$ gives $x=y$. The inverses $b_s:D_+(s)\to X_s\hookrightarrow X$ agree on overlaps. Indeed, over $D_+(s)\cap D_+(t)$, the equality $a\circ b_t=\mathrm{id}$ and $a^{-1}(D_+(s))=X_s$ make $b_t$ factor through $X_s$; it is then the inverse of $a_s$ restricted to this overlap, hence equals $b_s$. By lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing they glue to $b:V\to X$. The equalities $a b=\mathrm{id}_V$ and $b a=\mathrm{id}_X$ hold on the displayed open covers and hence globally by the uniqueness clause of the same lemma. Thus $X\simeq V$ through $a$. As $V$ is open in $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, this is an open immersion by def-weil-open-immersion. Under step 3 it is precisely the required $r:X\to P$.
